summary: Du et al. 2023 (arXiv:2305.14325v1, 'Preprint. Under review', PDF p1) propose that multiple instances of the same LLM independently answer a query, then iteratively update their answers after seeing other agents' concatenated responses (short/long consensus prompts, Fig 3, PDF p4), converging to a shared final answer. TASKS (six, all gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, zero-shot; eval details PDF p13): reasoning — (1) Arithmetic (six random integers 0–30 in a+b*c+d-e*f; 100 tasks, PDF pp5,13), (2) GSM8K (100 problems, PDF pp5,13), (3) Chess Move Prediction (best 15th move after 14 PGN moves; Stockfish pawn score depth 20; 300 games, PDF pp5,13); factuality — (4) Biographies (new benchmark, 524 computer scientists, bullet facts vs Wikipedia ground truth scored by chatGPT yes/no/uncertain, PDF pp6,13), (5) MMLU (100 questions, PDF pp7,13), (6) Chess Move Validity (BIG-Bench chess-state tracking, PDF p7). BASELINES (PDF p5): Single Agent; Single Agent + Reflection; Multi-Agent (Majority) — majority vote over multiple agents' independent generations; debate uses identical starting prompt/model; majority baseline omitted for factuality tasks because responses aren't comparable (PDF p7). MAIN RESULTS (3 agents, 2 rounds, Table 1 PDF p6): Arithmetic 81.8±2.3 debate vs 69.0±4.6 majority, 67.0±4.7 single, 72.1±4.5 reflection; GSM8K 85.0±3.5 vs 81.0±3.9 majority, 77.0±4.2 single (reflection 75.0 hurts); Chess ΔPS 122.9±7.6 vs 102.2±6.2 majority, 91.4±10.6 single. So debate beats majority voting by ~13 points on arithmetic and ~21 pawn-score points on chess, but only ~4 points (within overlapping error bars) on GSM8K. FACTUALITY (Table 2 PDF p7): Biographies 73.8 vs 66.0 single; MMLU 71.1 vs 63.9; Chess Validity 45.2 vs 29.3; reflection underperforms single agent on MMLU (57.7). SCALING: headline config is 3 agents/2 rounds 'due to computational expense', but accuracy rises with agents (1→5, with summarization for 5+) and rounds (1→4) (Fig 10, PDF pp5,8); longer/stubborner prompts slow convergence but improve final accuracy (Fig 12, PDF p8); summarizing other agents' responses improves over concatenation (Fig 13, PDF p8); personas raise MMLU 71.1→74.2 (PDF p8); ChatGPT+Bard debate on 20 GSM8K problems: Bard 11, ChatGPT 14, debate 17 (PDF pp8-9). CONSENSUS: convergence to a single answer is not guaranteed in theory but observed empirically; agents are 'relatively agreeable', attributed to instruction tuning/RLHF (PDF p4); uncertain facts produce divergent initial answers that debate collapses to one 'more accurate, but not necessarily always factually correct' answer (Fig 9, PDF p8); confidently-held facts resist persuasion, so 'ease of persuasion' is proposed as a confidence probe (PDF p7); short prompts yield faster consensus (Fig 14, PDF p13); debate can flip all-initially-wrong populations to correct (PDF pp2,6). FAILURE MODES: debate sometimes converges to a wrong value that agents confidently affirm (PDF p10 limitations; incorrect-debate examples Figs 21-23, PDF p13); long debates cause models to attend only to recent generations (PDF p10). COMPUTE: the paper concedes debate is 'more costly, requiring multiple model instances and rounds' (PDF p2) and 'more computationally expensive' than other prompting techniques (PDF p10); it reports NO compute-matched comparison — majority voting at 3 agents costs ~3 generations vs debate's ~9 (3 initial + 6 updates), so the debate-vs-majority gap is confounded by roughly 3x inference compute (my inference from the procedure, PDF p4; the paper never quantifies tokens).
unresolved: Exact per-condition token/cost accounting is absent from the paper — the magnitude of the compute confound can only be bounded procedurally (~3x at headline config), not measured.

Figure 10's per-point values for agent/round scaling are only available as axis descriptions in the text extraction (agents 1-5, performance ~70-90; rounds 1-4, ~70-85), so the exact shape (monotonic? saturating?) cannot be quoted numerically.
Whether debate's gains survive matching total generations to majority voting is not testable from this paper alone — this is the crux requiring the Smit et al. and Zhang et al. investigations.
The 20-problem ChatGPT+Bard result (PDF pp8-9) is anecdotal in size and has no error bars.
